input: am i connected to the internet
is this computer connected to the internet

tput cuu 1 && if ping -c 1 -W 2 1.1.1.1 > /dev/null 2>&1; then printf "\r

arguments.command:
tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Please choose a network diagnostic option" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
1) 📡 Ping a Host
2) 🛣️ Trace Route

Select diagnostic 1-2: " && read -r netchoice && case "$netchoice" in 1) termy_say "Please enter the target host" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "Target host: " && read -r host && if [ -n "$host" ]; then ping -c 3 "$host" && printf "
" && termy_say "Ping completed" > /dev/null 2>&1; else printf "
⛔ Host cannot be empty.
" && termy_say "Operation cancelled" > /dev/null 2>&1; fi ;; 2) termy_say "Please enter the target host" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "Target host: " && read -r host && if [ -n "$host" ]; then traceroute "$host" && printf "
" && termy_say "Traceroute completed" > /dev/null 2>&1; else printf "
⛔ Host cannot be empty.
" && termy_say "Operation cancelled" > /dev/null 2>&1; fi ;; *) printf "
⛔ Invalid selection.
" && termy_say "Invalid selection" > /dev/null 2>&1 ;; esac
arguments.explanation: Provides a menu for network diagnostics, allowing the user to ping a host or perform a traceroute.

input: check if a port is open
check if a port is in use
check if a port is listening
how to check if port is open

arguments.command:
tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Please enter the port number" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
🌐 Enter port number: " && read -r target_port && if [ -n "$target_port" ]; then printf "
Checking port %s...
" "$target_port" && if command -v ss > /dev/null 2>&1; then ss -lntp "sport = :$target_port"; else lsof -i :"$target_port"; fi && printf "
Analysis for port \033[1m%s\033[22m completed.
" "$target_port" && termy_say "Port analysis completed" > /dev/null 2>&1; else printf "
⛔ Port number cannot be empty.
" && termy_say "Operation cancelled" > /dev/null 2>&1; fi
arguments.explanation: Checks if a specified port is open and displays the process using it.

arguments.command:
OUTPUT_TXT=$(ss -tuln | awk 'NR>1 {split($4, a, ":"); print a[length(a)]}' | sort -nu | awk '{print "- Port: \033[1m" $1 "\033[22m"}') && COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT_TXT" | grep -c 'Port:') && tput cuu 1 && printf "
🌐 \033[1mActive Listening Ports:\033[22m
%s
" "$OUTPUT_TXT" && termy_say "Found $COUNT active listening ports" > /dev/null 2>&1
arguments.explanation: Displays a list of active listening network ports.
